Feature: zmx: CLI agents inside zmx sessions
Description: CLI agents running inside a zmx session are detected, from the variables zmx sets, the foreground process it reports on attach, or the attach command line.

Feature: zmx: session list in the SSH host editor
Description: The SSH host editor lists the zmx sessions on the server, with what each one is running, to pick the one to attach to after connecting.

Feature: zmx: switch sessions from a pane
Description: A pane attached to a zmx session offers the host's other sessions in its context menu, listed afresh each time the menu opens.
The settings dropdown no longer shows "User defined" for the Tab key behavior after it is refreshed.
A CLI agent such as Codex made the default in the new session menu is launched in new tabs and panes, instead of the built-in agent view.
With secret redaction on, secrets are masked in every request sent to an agent provider, not only on screen.
A pane shows what is sent to an agent provider and what comes back.
A profile can replace each prompt with a built-in or a custom template from ~/.zap/prompts, re-read on every request.

Feature: BYOP: disabling providers and filtering models
Description: An agent provider can be disabled instead of removed, and the models it offers can be filtered.
A copy of the models.dev catalog is built in, for when it can't be downloaded.
An Ollama provider's models get their context windows from Ollama.
An edit whose search text matches more than one place is refused rather than applied to one of them, and a loose match is reported to the model.
A running command's card has a Stop button, and a command waiting for approval an Explain button, whose request is redacted and shown in the request inspector.
A tool call with invalid arguments shows as a failed call.
A very long answer is cut short behind a button that shows the rest, and a BYOP compaction summary shows as a collapsed marker.
A long multi-line command that the shell would run line by line asks first.
Connections through the ssh wrapper get keepalives when none is configured.

Feature: SSH: splits on the same host
Description: Splitting a pane that is in an SSH session opens the new pane on the same host.
The SSH extension asks before installing on a host where a first install failed, instead of installing silently as an update.
The SSH extension checks the SHA-256 of what it downloads, which only releases made since publish.

Releases are published from this repository, and auto-update, the about page and the remote server download point here. A release is created only once every platform has built (macOS on Apple silicon and Intel, Linux x86_64). The DMGs, the AppImage and the CLI archives carry the release's version, as zap-<version>-<system>. Tags are v<YYYY>.<MM>.<DD>.<N>; the releases before the project became independent were numbered -mod.X.Y (v2026.07.09.2-mod.1.1 was the last), and a Zap of the withdrawn releases up to v2026.07.09.2-mod.3 has to be reinstalled once.
Only Linux and macOS are supported; Windows code, assets and scripts are removed.
The release builds the Arch package, and both it and the .deb declare the libraries the binary links against and the oldest glibc it runs on, read from the binary when it is packaged.
zap for pacman, zap-deb for Pacstall and the cask zap-terminal for Homebrew, from q0wkp/pkgs, which the release workflow asks to package each release.

Zap installed with pacman from q0wkp/pkgs, with Pacstall or with the Homebrew cask updates itself through that package manager, once q0wkp/pkgs has published the release there; other installs show the command that installs the new one.
The release workflow is this project's own; upstream's other workflows, issue and pull request templates and Dependabot settings are removed.
The crates outside app/ pass their own unit tests.
Crashes and panics in the terminal grid, font loading, the Markdown parser and pane cleanup.

Testing a connection and listing zmx sessions hand the password or the key's passphrase to ssh through an askpass helper, so a correct password is no longer reported as wrong and a key with a passphrase can be tested.

Feature: SSH manager: host keys and input checks
Description: The SSH manager asks before trusting an unknown host key, and rejects hosts, users and ports that ssh would misread.

Feature: SSH manager: deleting and cloning hosts
Description: Deleting a saved host or folder asks for confirmation, and a host is deleted and cloned together with its keychain secrets.

Feature: SSH manager and SFTP: hover redraws
Description: Hovering over the SSH manager's tree, the OneKey manager and the SFTP browser's breadcrumb, context menu and cancel buttons no longer renders the view again without end.
A file link opens in the session of the block it is in, not in the active block's session.
The wrapper that turns off the pager for an agent's command closes on a line of its own where the command has several lines or a comment.
The database connection opened ahead of startup is always used, instead of being dropped when its thread finished first.

Anthropic streams with content blocks other than text, thinking and tool use no longer end in an error, and their usage is not counted twice; every tool call of an OpenAI stream message is emitted, with its id and index kept; Gemini tool calls get unique ids and their responses the function's name.

Feature: BYOP: tool calls written as text
Description: A tool call a model writes into its reply text runs only when the whole reply is nothing but calls to tools offered in the request; a call that is quoted, explained or names an unknown tool no longer runs.

A Zap built from a release installs the SSH extension only when the release signed the SHA-256 of its download: the release workflow signs each SHA-256 file, and Zap checks the signature before the remote host checks the download.

Feature: Editor: multi-line text in a heading
Description: Pasting several lines into a heading inserts each line once.
A launch configuration whose pane branch has no panes fails to parse, instead of crashing the app when opened.
Hovering over a notebook's file path tooltip or a checkbox of the MCP update modal no longer renders the view again without end.

Feature: Vim: inner block and paragraph objects
Description: ci{ on a block holding only a newline, and ip and ap on the blank lines at the start of a buffer, no longer produce a range that starts after its end.
A wildcard pattern with many * that fails late no longer stalls file search, and ? stands for one character everywhere.

Feature: sum_tree: seeking past the last item
Description: A seek past a subtree's last item counts that item once.
A shell that can't be executed is reported as an error instead of a blank pane, and a failed start no longer leaves the PTY's descriptor open.

Feature: Links: URLs wrapped by the program
Description: A URL that a program broke with its own line break at the last column is detected whole.

Feature: Warp fixes: current user and secret redaction
Description: The current user is found without a passwd entry and with a long directory (LDAP/AD) entry, and the secret redaction rules are swapped as one value, which removes a deadlock.
A placement with nothing to draw is ignored instead of panicking or scrolling without end, and replies use the protocol's error codes and carry the placement id.

Feature: Kitty graphics: delete specifiers and image numbers
Description: Every delete specifier that selects placements is handled, where anything but a and i used to delete every image, and images can be transmitted and addressed by number.
Images placed through Unicode placeholders are shown, which is how tmux passes images through.

Feature: File watcher: moves into and out of the tree
Description: A path moved out of the watched tree is reported as deleted and one moved in as added.
A logger that takes over a log file waits for the previous one to finish writing.
The preferences file is replaced by a rename, so a crash or a full disk no longer leaves it truncated.

Feature: WarpUI: aborted futures and view tracking
Description: A spawned future never resolves after it was aborted, and a render that panics no longer leaves its view tracked.

Feature: Warp fixes: MCP config files, voice input and weak handles
Description: An MCP config file that can't be read or parsed keeps its servers running, cancelling voice input drops the recording being processed, and a weak handle no longer upgrades once the last strong handle is dropped.
